full_judgment: The dispute between the parties relates to a piece of land measuring 0.02¾ acres. It will be referred to, hereinafter, as the case land. It is situated on plot No. 50794, appertaining to MRR Khatian No. 1328, corresponding to PS Khatian No. 1319 in Mouza Char King, previously known as Char Ishwar. This will be referred to, in the' paragraphs that follow as the case holding. One Moqbul Ahmed had owned 0.50 acres of land in the case holding. He died leaving behind a family, comprising his widow, 6 sons and 2 daughters, to succeed him to his estate. Ruhul Amin and Abdul Matin are two of his sons. On 14-9-1989 Ruhul Amin sold 0.02 acres of land from the case holding to Mohammad Abdul Mannan, who thus became a co-sharer by purchase of the case holding. He is the opposite party No. 1 of the instant civil revision. He is an Advocate. He built on the land so purchased a 'baithakkhana', though not as an adjunct to any dwelling quarter. On 4-3-1990 Abdul Matin sold 0.02¾ acres of land from the 'case holding' to Md Madinullah Miah, a stranger to the case holding. This is the case land. This is contiguous to the land held by Mannan and lies next to his 'baithakkhana', This gave Mannan an occasion to file, almost 7 years later an application for pre-emption of the case land and institute the Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1997. It was under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950. He impleaded in it Md Madinullah Miah, the purchaser of the case land as the pre-emptee opposite party No. 1 and Abdul Matin, the vendor of the 'case land' as the vendor opposite party No. 2. Abdul Matin is the opposite party No. 2 in the instant civil revision. He was also a party in the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 59 of 2000.out of which the present civil revision arose. The appeal was against the judgment and order passed in the said Miscellaneous Case No.4 of 1997. Abdul Matin took no part in the proceedings, either in the Courts below or in this Court.
